name: Centrepoint — Devco affordable/workforce-housing redesign (filed as H-2024-0019; marketed "Centrepoint")
location: SW corner N Eagle Rd & W Ustick Rd — 3100 N Centrepoint Way / 3030 N Cajun Ln, Meridian ID (~4.9-5.0 mi from subject, near the ring edge)
reason: Meridian P&Z recommended DENIAL of Devco's deed-restricted affordable redesign (down from an ~2022 market-rate mixed-use plan of ~365 units on the same site). City Council overrode P&Z 3-1 and approved it with modifications on 12/10/2024 (Council Member Liz Strader dissenting) — five flat-roofed buildings, 1-3 stories. On 5/27/2025 Devco cancelled the affordable version outright, publicly citing loss of competitive LIHTC tax credits and loss of key HUD program eligibility that made the financing "unsustainable."
revival_risk: Low + the LIHTC/HUD financing window that killed this specific affordable product is unlikely to reopen soon; NOTE the site itself is not dead — land reverted to the prior ~2022-approved market-rate plan (213 units), which is already the live roster entry in this project's Supply Chart (permits issuing 2026). This entry documents only the killed affordable-housing product, a gap not previously captured in repo files.
note: This is a genuinely new find, not in the existing register: the repo's Supply Chart tracks the live 213-unit market-rate Centrepoint (Dec 2025 approval), but nowhere documents the P&Z-denial-recommendation + Council-override + 2025 developer-withdrawal chain that killed the interim affordable-housing design at the same address. Worth noting for underwriting: Meridian lost a below-market-rent product at this corner (net-neutral to slightly negative for competitive market-rate supply at the subject, since the site converts entirely into market-rate units instead of a mixed affordable/market pipeline).
sources: Idaho Statesman, "Affordable apartments axed in Meridian," ~May 27, 2025 (content via search-engine snippet; idahostatesman.com blocks direct fetch, per known CLAUDE.md limitation)
BoiseDev/Idaho Press coverage of the Meridian City Council 12/10/2024 vote on H-2024-0019 (content via search-engine snippet; boisedev.com 403s direct fetch)

name: Unnamed apartment rezone (filed as "houses"/subdivision in first 2022 attempt, refiled as apartments in 2024) — no confirmed marketed brand found; team's working label "Lake Hazel & Five Mile MF"
location: Unincorporated Ada County, "Southwest Boise" area — reported at/near Lake Hazel Rd & Five Mile Rd per the team's known register (task brief). BoiseDev's own text describes it only as "an empty commercial lot just outside of Southwest Boise" / "a commercial lot ... in Southwest Boise" — I could not independently pull the parcel address, APN, or precise intersection this session (see verification note below). Straight-line distance from subject estimated ~5 mi based on the SW Boise/SWACA area's general footprint (Cole Rd east / Five Mile-Maple Grove west / I-84 north / Lake Hazel-Kuna Rd south) — close to the 5.2 mi cutoff; NOT independently confirmed with coordinates.
reason: Neighborhood opposition to density ("hearing opposition towards high density" per BoiseDev headline). The Ada County Board of County Commissioners denied the site for residential use TWICE: first a for-sale housing/subdivision proposal (~128u per team register, denial reported ~2022, article not independently located this session), then on Wed 5/22/2024 they "voted for a second time" to turn down an apartment proposal (~118u per team register) on the same parcel. revival_risk: Low — the parcel's entitlement path is now commercial (approved Oct 2025), and Ada County separately rolled back allowing multifamily as a use in commercial zones in its zoning-code rewrite (per BoiseDev 4/11/2025, "Ada County rolls back multi-family housing in commercial zones ... after public input"), which would make a third MF attempt on this specific parcel harder going forward, not easier.
